structure: Part 15 read src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/journey-spec.json (2814 lines) and spec/fixtures/happy-path.json (one line). The specification has seven top-level keys: specVersion 1; journey high-risk-plants-import-notification; 7 sources (policy paper, Confluence user needs, Confluence requirements, mural, design prototype, live animals frontend, skeleton); 98 behaviours, each with id, source, status, detail and an optional ruling decision; one fieldGroup (address); 8 sections (start, commodity, origin, arrival, destination, parties, contact, review) with a gate, title and pages, each page with its pattern, caption, route, collects and notes; and 29 obligations, each with its level (appliesAt), kind, mandate, input widget, values and format, label, hint, error copy, enforcement at continue, animals relation and ruled notes. The happy-path fixture is one line, schema_version 1 with an empty values object. Claims run in file order: sources, behaviours, sections and pages, the address field group, obligations, then the fixture, plus inferred and gap claims where the specification and the pages disagree or the specification states something no page implements. Since the earlier extract at a88175f the only change in this slice is that the persistence port's finalise operation is now named submit (records.submit, stub submit) in behaviours persistence-mapper-a-only, mi-metrics-eight, live-access-synchronous-submission and nfr-available-24x7-and-load and in obligations dateOfNotification and lateNotificationIndicator; every earlier claim is kept, with its quote brought up to the current verbatim text.

claims.quote: A notification therefore carries exactly one commodityType chosen first; a mixed consignment is two notifications. The commodity-type hint says so.

claims.quote: the trail keeps the newest 40 places, past which the oldest drop and Back ends at the Overview

claims.quote: Ware potatoes from Spain/Poland; Ware potatoes from Spain/Portugal with a late notification; Seed potatoes from any EU country; Spruce (Picea) from any EU country; Conifer wood from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain

claims.statement: The previous notification scheme and the Northern Irish and Irish services can only refine wording and value lists later, never change what the notification collects, because the statutory list fixes that.
claims.quote: Annex 2 equals the SI matters, so the previous scheme cannot change WHAT is collected.

claims.statement: Because the policy paper is a draft, every list is data behind the commodities service, each timing window is a single named constant read by the lateness rule and any hint that quotes it, and the territory wording and authority names are copy, so a policy change is a data or copy change rather than a model change.
claims.quote: the timing windows POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL = 2 (reg 24A(1)) and PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL = 4 (reg 26(1)) are exported from one module beside the arrival-details feature and are the only place a window is written

claims.statement: Checks are made without prior notice, so the journey holds no check booked step, appointment slot or inspection date, and a post-arrival trader may give a current location instead of the destination, which is why the arrival status and the destination are captured together.
claims.quote: Policy also notes a post-arrival notifier may give a current location instead of the destination, so a check may happen elsewhere than first notified — that is why arrivalStatus + placeOfDestination are captured together.

claims.statement: The name of the person making the entry is read as the name on the contact address the trader picked, rather than the signed-in user's own name.

claims.quote: First pass: picker only, same as animals — the trader adds the consignor in the INS address book first; the pick is copied onto the notification and Edit details changes that copy for this notification only (EUDPA-662).

claims.quote: Seed potatoes | Ware potatoes | Plants for planting | Trees for planting | Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer | Conifer wood without bark (from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain) | Cut coniferous trees more than 3 metres high | Wood of sweet chestnut, ash or plane that keeps all or part of its natural round surface | Wood of sweet chestnut, ash or plane in chips not processed into pellets or briquettes

claims.quote: For example, 250. Give the number of plants, tubers, trees or units of wood as a whole number.

claims.statement: A potato line must give its intended use as free text of up to 58 characters, hinted with the examples planting, processing or fresh sale, because no source supplies a list of options.

claims.statement: A plants for planting or trees for planting line must give the EPPO code for the plant, free text of up to 58 characters hinted with the example QUERO for Quercus robur.
claims.quote: The EPPO code for the plant. For example, QUERO for Quercus robur.
